description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on do while loop statements in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
i starts at 1 and j at 2; both become non-zero after the increments, so Convert.ToBoolean is true and true && true prints True. The loop runs while i <= 3, i.e. three times (k is unused).

Output:

True
True
True

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
The body always runs once. i++ uses 1.0f (then i becomes 2.0f) and ++j makes j 1.05f. 1.0f - 1.05f is a float value around -0.04999995. Then i < 2.0f is false, so the loop stops.

Output:

-0.04999995

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
The right-hand side i++ * j uses the old i, then i is incremented, then the product is assigned back to i. First: 1 * 5 = 5. Second: 5 * 5 = 25. 25 <= 10 is false, so the loop ends.

Output:

5
25

questions.question: For the incomplete C# program below, which of the C# code fragment will not result in an infinite loop?
questions.explanation: Only option a updates i (i = i / 10) until i becomes 0, so it terminates and j is the digit sum 10. Option b never changes i, and option c keeps i % 10 == 4, so both loop forever. Option d does not compile: (i / 10 == 0) is bool, and bool != int is illegal.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?

questions.explanation: Each iteration prints x % 10 (the least significant digit) then divides x by 10. For 1234 the console shows 4, 3, 2, 1 — the digits in reverse order.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?

options.text: It finds binary equivalent of i
It finds octal equivalent of i
It finds sum of digits of i

questions.explanation: 2 * 4 is 8, so the loop repeatedly takes i % 8 and i / 8 while shifting the place value a by * 10. That is the decimal writing of the octal digits of i. For 342 the printed value is 526 (342 octal).

questions.question: What is the correct syntax for do while loop?
questions.explanation: A do-while must end with while (condition); including the semicolon. Option c is missing that semicolon and will not compile.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
A do-while always runs its body once. WriteLine(x++) prints 10. Convert.ToBoolean(0) is false, so the && chain is false and the loop does not repeat.

Output:

10

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
The for-loop runs for x = 10 through 15 (six times). Each time the do-while prints 1; continue jumps to while (false), so that inner loop ends, then break leaves the while. Six 1s are printed.

Output:

1
1
1
1
1
1

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
Each time j starts at 1 and the do-while increments it to 2. Then x % 2 == 2 is false for x = 1, 2, and 3, so j stays 2.

Output:

1 2
2 2
3 2
